summary.headline: Tega Q4 FY26: FY26 revenue up 5% to INR17,736 mn, adjusted EBITDA 22%; consumables flat as orders slipped to Feb–Mar, and Molycop acquisition closed 1 June 2026.
summary.overview: Tega reported FY26 revenue of INR17,736 mn (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR3,967 mn (22% margin), after exceptional items of INR775 mn (Molycop deal costs) and INR64 mn (labour code), with a further INR839 mn total labour-code charge cited. Consumables revenue was flat for the year, with Q4 consumables revenue down INR162 mn YoY, which management attributed to orders landing late in Q3/Q4 and shipping delays from container and vessel constraints. Equipment grew 25% to INR2,688 mn for FY26. The Molycop acquisition completed on 1 June 2026 with Apollo Funds as a minority partner; consolidation starts from Q1 FY27, and management flagged about USD30 mn of transaction costs payable in Q1 and a target of 3x leverage in 3 to 4 years.

segments.name: Consumables (Tega)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue flat YoY (FY24 +10%, FY25 +11%); Q4 revenue INR4,406 mn vs INR4,568 mn. Management says Q4 consumables EBITDA margin normally runs 27–28%, and an analyst estimated 27.7% excluding the INR776 mn one-off.

segments.name: Equipment (Tega)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR2,688 mn, +25% YoY; Q4 revenue up INR69 mn (+9%). Management guides 25% growth in FY27 and 12–13% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Molycop (grinding media, acquired 1 June 2026)
segments.commentary: Management's FY26 (July–June) estimate: revenue ~USD1,539 mn in the prior year, ~1% growth and ~12% EBITDA margin. FY27 planning assumption of ~3% growth, under reassessment.

guidance_outlook: Consumables: management reiterates 15%+ long-term CAGR; FY27 Equipment growth of about 25% and 12–13% Equipment EBITDA margin.
Blended group EBITDA margin guided at 21–22%, held despite FY26 at the low end.
Molycop acquisition costs of about USD30 mn to be paid in Q1 FY27; more deal costs possible in later quarters.
Molycop FY27 maintenance capex budgeted at USD20 mn; growth capex not yet factored in. Chile plant capex of USD25–30 mn to complete in FY27.
Sustaining and modernisation capex for Tega of INR50–60 crore, funded from internal accruals.
Synergy framework (revenue synergies at Tega, cost synergies at Molycop, non-core asset sales) is being re-evaluated; 100-day and 200-day plans in progress; no numbers yet.
capex_capacity: Chile plant: civil works about 50–60% complete; commissioning targeted for early Q3 FY27, subject to regulatory approvals. Revenue booking may start end of Q4 FY27 or slip to FY28.

Acquisition debt: about USD838 mn of Molycop debt consolidated from 1 June (down from over USD1,050 mn after about USD220 mn paydown); INR1,500 crore raised at the parent level from Standard Chartered, Axis and EXIM, already drawn.
Molycop capex about 2–3% of revenue; management says it is cash-flow funded with no new borrowing needed.
Tega sustaining capex INR50–60 crore a year, funded from internal accruals; Chile funded from accruals and existing borrowings.
demand_pricing: Order book INR12,060 mn at 31 March 2026, of which INR9,060 mn executable within 12 months; pending orders up about 18% YoY (17% in another reference).
Q4 orders came mainly in February and March, so revenue lags 3–6 months given bespoke design-led execution.

Consumables shipments were held up by Middle East disruption (vessel and container availability), lifting finished goods by about INR50 crore, equal to about INR100 crore of potential revenue; alternate routes being sought.
Market backdrop cited: gold demand above 5,000 tonnes in CY2025; copper demand growth about 3% vs supply about 2%.
Molycop FY27 growth may be weaker than the earlier ~7–8% view, as Cobre Panama and Grasberg restarts are now expected in FY28 rather than FY27.

qa_highlights.question: When will Molycop be consolidated, and how much debt is added?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation starts 1 June 2026, with the first full quarter in Q1 FY27 (one month of Molycop). About USD838 mn of debt is added at the group level, and INR1,500 crore of parent-level debt was already raised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consumables revenue stay flat when guidance was ~8% and the 15% CAGR has been missed in recent years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed late-quarter order intake and logistics disruption. It said the 15% long-term CAGR guidance still holds, citing cyclicality, and that executable orders are up about 17%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Molycop acquisition cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD30 mn of acquisition and financing-related costs will be paid in Q1 FY27, including debt refinancing and preference costs. Management says these are one-offs and not a loss, and more costs may follow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chile capex of USD25–30 mn completes in FY27, Tega sustaining capex is INR50–60 crore, and Molycop maintenance capex is USD20 mn. Growth capex is not yet set.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 25% Equipment growth in FY27 and what is the new product?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a new aggregate product with a Japanese partner to launch in Q3 FY27, plus tailwinds from capex, power and mineral beneficiation, and export pushes into Canada, CIS and the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital improve, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Payables improved and debtor days fell. Management guides 100–105 days DSO to be maintained, with absolute receivables varying with sales volume.

risks_watch: Consumables execution: Q4 shortfall and FG build-up of about INR50 crore need to convert to revenue in Q1–Q2 FY27.
Molycop integration, synergy quantification and deleveraging to 3x within 3–4 years.
Further Molycop acquisition costs in Q1 FY27 and beyond; reported profit could be depressed in the consolidated P&L.
Chile plant commissioning slipping because of regulatory approvals, which would push revenue into FY28.
Molycop volume recovery deferred from FY27 to FY28, with uncertainty over the 3% FY27 growth assumption.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book and long-term demand, but defensive on the consumables shortfall, which management attributed to timing and logistics. Vague on Molycop numbers and synergies, with several answers deferred to later quarters.
key_quotes: So the revenue is kind of a timing issue because most of the orders came in February and March.
Molycop has a financial year ending at 30th June.
We remain firm on our guidance of 15% plus on a long-term basis.
